$schema: Verification register. One entry per topic: what was checked, against what, and what is still open. Status values: 'reference-checked' (the specific claims listed in 'checked' were compared with the cited reference), 'engine-tested' (forms are generated by code and compared with hand-written expected forms in the automated tests), 'author-written' (written from standard reference-grammar knowledge but not yet compared line by line with a cited source), 'needs-review' (known open questions). No entry has been reviewed by a native speaker or a qualified teacher.
statement: No native speaker, Italian teacher or linguist has reviewed this course. Statements marked 'reference-checked' were compared with the named references by the author of the content; everything else is the author's own work based on standard grammar and should be treated as unreviewed. Corrections are welcome.

references.title: Passato remoto
references.author: Eva Wiberg
references.checked: -ei/-etti alternatives (vendei o vendetti); narrative (foreground) function; regional Italian largely mirrors dialect usage; strong preference for the passato remoto in Sicilian, Calabrian and Salentine dialect areas.

references.title: Passato prossimo
references.author: Eva Wiberg
references.checked: Aoristic passato prossimo spreading from the North, except in Tuscany; in the South the passato remoto is used where the standard would have the passato prossimo.

references.title: Participio
references.author: Verner Egerland
references.checked: Agreement with a preceding direct-object clitic, especially 3rd person; less regular with 1st/2nd person (ci hanno visti / visto); agreement with relative che no longer standard (literary, antiquated, dialectal); participio assoluto. The article does not discuss ne.

references.title: Periodo ipotetico
references.author: Michele Prandi
references.checked: Three standard types (reality, possibility, unreality); substandard double imperfetto, attested in Dante, Machiavelli, Manzoni; conditional in the protasis non-standard ('doppio condizionale').

references.title: Congiuntivo
references.author: Michele Prandi
references.checked: Indicativo for congiuntivo in completive clauses = lower register, same meaning; in restrictive relatives the mood choice changes the meaning.

references.title: La scelta degli ausiliari (consulenza linguistica)
references.author: Accademia della Crusca
references.checked: Modal + essere-verb: both sono dovuto andare and ho dovuto andare acceptable; avere with essere or a passive infinitive; clitic before the modal → essere (non ci sono voluti andare). The link points to the consultation index; search it for the title.

references.title: Verbi servili (entry on the auxiliary of modal verbs)
references.author: DICO — Dubbi sull'italiano consulenza online, Università di Messina
references.checked: Modal takes the auxiliary of the infinitive; reports Serianni's view that avere is required when the infinitive is essere. Serianni's Grammatica italiana was not consulted directly.

Forms tested. Uses (epistemic future, reportative conditional, future in the past) are author-written. 'sperare che + futuro' is mentioned as an alternative and has not been checked against a reference.

All texts are original and every word is checked automatically against the dictionary. Naturalness of the Italian has not been reviewed by a native speaker.

Heuristic: it lists every dictionary analysis of a form and chooses one by context; it refuses sentences with unknown words. Its choices are tested on a fixed set of sentences only, and it can be wrong on others.
